title: Oklahoma's 47-Game Winning Streak (1953-57): How It Began and Ended
question: What is the longest winning streak in college football history?
answer: Oklahoma won 47 straight games from October 1953 to November 1957 under Bud Wilkinson, the longest winning streak in Division I history. Notre Dame ended it 7-0 in Norman on Nov. 16, 1957.
summary: Oklahoma's record 47-game winning streak ran from 1953 to 1957 under Bud Wilkinson before Notre Dame ended it 7-0 in Norman. Here's how it started and stopped.
body: The most famous run in college football history didn't start the way you'd expect. Bud Wilkinson's 1953 Sooners opened with a 28-21 home loss to top-ranked Notre Dame, then played to a 7-7 tie at Pittsburgh. On Oct. 10, 1953, they beat Texas 19-14 in Dallas. Oklahoma would not lose again for more than four years.

During those years the Sooners won back-to-back national championships in 1955 and 1956. The 1956 team was especially dominant and went to South Bend to beat Notre Dame 40-0. That rout helps explain why so few people expected the Irish to cause trouble the following year.

The streak ended on Nov. 16, 1957, at Owen Field. Notre Dame had lost its previous two games, to Navy and Michigan State, and came to Norman as a heavy underdog. Oklahoma drove deep into Irish territory three times and came away empty each time. Late in the fourth quarter Notre Dame faced fourth down at the OU 3. Halfback Dick Lynch took a pitch and followed fullback Nick Pietrosante's block into the end zone for the only touchdown of the day. Terry Brennan's Irish held on to win 7-0, and Oklahoma's last drive ended on an interception in the end zone.

The Sooners regrouped and won their last three games, including a 48-21 Orange Bowl win over Duke, to finish 10-1. Those 47 straight victories still stand as the longest winning streak in Division I history, and no team has seriously threatened the mark.
